title.narrative: Number of private sector actors and individuals reached by communication campaign

description.narrative: This indicator monitors the number of actors from private sector (including employers, employees and their professional organizations, etc.), youth and their families who are the target group of adult and apprenticeship trainings to be reached through communication campaign that covers facetoface activities as well as social media engagement and interactions. Persons reached by those channels will be counted under the indicator target value. An integrated and nationwide communication campaign will be developed to raise the interest of the public concerning the negative social and economic consequences of child labour, the benefits brought by apprenticeship training and its contribution to combat child labour.Using various media and articulated with sociocultural activities, the communication campaign will be implemented in whole programme duration. Communication activities, including the physical meetings and information material, will permit to disseminate messages and sensitization material regarding child labour and the benefits of apprenticeship to offer a safer and more sustainable market insertion to the youth, as well as information material to give practical and accurate information about the VET trainings available, the local jobs these trainings prepare for and the different prerequisites.Besides, campaigns on the social media channels will be conducted to share key messages in line with the measures of the programme. Media/ Social media monitoring will be carried out through the voice/reach/engagement methodology which is further elaborated in the Communication and Visibility Plan of the programme. As a result of the discussions made at the latest management meeting in January 2023 where the EUD PM also took place as a member (ref: Meeting minutes of the Technical Committee Meeting dated 18/01/2023), it has been agreed that number of people who visit the VET4JOB website and other social media channels and engaged with posts/shares would be reported under the communication campaign indicator. With this agreement, monitoring and reporting of the beneficiaries reached by the communication campaign has become twofold: 1) Number of persons reached by facetoface communication activities and informative visits/interactions. Below reported figures cover the beneficiaries interacted in such activities which are developed and implemented in line with the communication campaign strategy. These activities will continue particularly at the vocational training institutions and be extended to all programme provinces in the course of the programme duration.2) The second approach to reach beneficiaries is through VET4JOB social media channels and programme website by carrying out social media campaigns and engagement. Engagement is defined as likes, posts/reposts or tweets or story created, follows, commentsetc. Overall, it is the intended interaction between the users and accounts. Social media engagement figures are counted under the output indicator related to communication campaign.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries provided with career guidance services and RPL support

description.narrative: This indicator monitors the number of beneficiaries (youth and adults) who benefited from career guidance services and RPL supports to be provided by training institutions. Turkish and Syrian adults, who have professional skills but have not been able to certify this, will be provided consulting services to certify their qualifications. Providing RPL guidance cover:Those who have a professional skill which is in the scope of the apprenticeship training will be ensured to continue the apprenticeship education system by performing equivalence procedures.Those with skills in occupations covered by VQA will be directed to VQA exams. If the required number is reached, VQA will be provided to conduct Arabic examinations for Syrian migrants.Adults who have professional skills which are neither in the scope of apprenticeship training nor VQA, will be directed to journeyman and master craftsman exams held by TESKs suborganizations and thus will be supported to have valid certificates. Providing logistical support for RPL cover preparatory courses to be organized for adults who will take VQA exams. These courses, which will be opened with the aim of increasing the success of the participants, will include the topics such as; introduction of the VQA system, the features of the exams, the points to be considered in the exams, etc. Furthermore, financial support will be provided for the constraints (such as transfer to the place of exam, fee of exam, etc.) that prevent them from taking the exams.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries who received work permits with the support of the programme

description.narrative: The relevant indicator is formulated to track the number of Syrian beneficiaries who received work permits with the support of the programme. However, each work permit is valid for a year and it has to be renewed annually for the same person. And thus irrespective of individuals, the same procedural and financial support by the programme have to be invested. Therefore under this indicator number of work permits issued for Syrians with the technical and/or financial support of the programme is agreed to be monitored and reported. This approach is also in line with the respective rRF indicator (LOc.04). Besides, GoT also announces number of permits issued. A work permit is issued by MoLSS (DG ILF) to employers and thus obtaining a work permit is beyond the responsibility of the programme. Provision of technical support means to facilitate procedures and documentation required in the application process. Provision of financial support means the payment of necessary fees for obtaining work permits. This type of support was not foreseen in the original programme design however as discussed and agreed with EUD, work permit fees are covered by the programme budget. For each work permit it costs the employer around 1,5002,000 TL.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries who received work permits with the support of the programme

description.narrative: The relevant indicator is formulated to track the number of Syrian beneficiaries who received work permits with the support of the programme. However, each work permit is valid for a year and it has to be renewed annually for the same person. And thus irrespective of individuals, the same procedural and financial support by the programme have to be invested. Therefore under this indicator number of work permits issued for Syrians with the technical and/or financial support of the programme is agreed to be monitored and reported. This approach is also in line with the respective rRF indicator (LOc.04). Besides, GoT also announces number of permits issued. A work permit is issued by MoLSS (DG ILF) to employers and thus obtaining a work permit is beyond the responsibility of the programme. Provision of technical support means to facilitate procedures and documentation required in the application process. Provision of financial support means the payment of necessary fees for obtaining work permits. This type of support was not foreseen in the original programme design however as discussed and agreed with EUD, work permit fees are covered by the programme budget. For each work permit it costs the employer around 1,5002,000 TL.
